{{Quote|Send out the Gorog!''"<br />"''But, my Lord, the arena's restraints&hellip; they haven't been properly tested!''"<br />"''Open the Gorog gate! Now!|Baron Merillion Tarko orders his Neimoidian aide to release the Gorog|<ref name="TFU2">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>}}
The '''Gorog''' was a gargantuan beast used in the [[Tarko-se Arena]] on [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]]. The immense, bipedal creature possessed a hunched stance, two human-like hands with opposable thumbs, two hearts, and four tusks protruding from its lower jaw. The Gorog was ordered released by [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]], against the advice of an [[Unidentified Neimoidian aide 1|aide]] concerned about the arena's untested restraint system, as a last-ditch effort to stop [[Subject 1138|Galen Marek's clone]] from rescuing [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] from the arena. This act of recklessness would prove fatal for Baron Tarko, as he was killed by the indiscriminate giant.<ref name="TFU2" />

==Attributes==
[[File:Starkiller_v_Gorog.png|thumb|250px|The Gorog's immense size in comparison to Starkiller|left]]
The Gorog was a creature of immense size,<ref name="TFU2" /> as big as the [[Tarko-se Arena]],<ref name=":0">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> despite possessing surprising speed.<ref name=":2">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> It was so big that it could easily capture<ref name="TFU2" /> and eat<ref name=":1">{{InsiderCite|121|The Good, the Bad, and the Gorog: The Art of Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II|The Good, the Bad, and the Gorog: The Art of ''Star Wars'': The Force Unleashed II}}</ref> adult [[Rancor/Legends|rancors]]. It had a large muscular midsection and forearms<ref name="TFU2" /> as thick as a small cruiser,<ref name=":2" /> while its upper arm and upper leg were more skeletal, with its gray leathery skin growing around the bone, creating a hole where the biceps or thigh, respectively, of most [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] would be. Its legs were small in comparison to the rest of its body, and included a hock ankle, making them appear more beast-like in the lower half than humanoid.<ref name="TFU2" />

Despite having a large [[Bone/Legends|cranium]], it didn't seemed to have much to fill it.<ref name=":0" /> The Gorog's head included<ref name="TFU2" /> an ugly<ref name=":0" /> humanoid face with sharp teeth and four large bone tusks protruding from the lower jaw. It had a metal plate on its head covering a large scar,<ref name="TFU2" /> where some genetic defect or wound had left its [[Brain/Legends|brain]] exposed.<ref name=":2" /> Chains and huge electromagnetic shackles were enough to keep the gigantic creature in captivity.<ref name="TFU2" /> The creature had notably two [[Heart/Legends|hearts]], and was capable of surviving even with just one still functioning.<ref name="TFU2comic" /> It had dark<ref name=":2" /> red blood,<ref name="TFU2comic" /> which taste seemed to enrage it.<ref name=":2" />

==History==

===Origins===
{{Quote|No time, General! What the hell is this thing?!''"<br />"''I have no idea, but it's big!''"<br />"''That's perceptive, for a blind man. Now how do I kill it?!''"<br />"''I'm not sure you can!|Starkiller and Kota argue about the Gorog|<ref name="TFU2" />}}
According to the religious text "[[Yorgalock]]" of the [[Reegau]] tribesmen, the first Gorog was made by a creator deity that attempted to create a being greater than itself. However, the Gorog crushed the Creator in its fist and immediately began scouring the land for food. The text warned that the Gorog was the "end of all things" and that "only those that hide in his shadow will survive."<ref>''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

===Clashing with Starkiller's clone===
By the times of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] an immense Gorog was held under the [[Tarko-se Arena]].<ref name="TFU2" /> In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]]<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II graphic novel">The [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' comic]] places the project in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].</ref> it was released by orders of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]] to confront the [[Subject 1138|clone]] of [[Galen Marek]], despite protests from a [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidian]] [[Unidentified Neimoidian aide 1|aide]] that the restraining devices intended to restrict the creature's movement while in the arena hadn't been completely tested. Indeed, during the clone Marek's fight with it, he trapped the Gorog's arms several times, but it repeatedly broke away from the restraints.<ref name="TFU2" />

Starkiller engaged the giant beast in combat, and quickly discovered that it possessed considerable power. It tried to smash him several times with its fists, but the clone was able to restrain it for a short time. After Starkiller attacked the Gorog's head, however, the creature became angry, broke free, and destroyed the arena's supports. Starkiller was able to escape and, along with [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], confronted Baron Tarko. However, the Gorog destroyed the platform they were on, killed the Baron, and grabbed [[General/Legends|General]] Kota. Following that, the Gorog fell into the arena. The entire structure collapsed under the creature's weight and also tumbled down<ref name="TFU2" /> the miles-long plunge to [[Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimodia]] below.<ref name=":0" />

Starkiller jumped after the creature and, after a longer struggle while falling, he was able to hurt the Gorog. He then used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to burst through the creature's torso, which caused the Gorog to release Kota from its grip.<ref name="TFU2" /> Muscular waves rolled back and forth, twisting him from side to side. The clone felt like a groundquake-a fleshquake on a planer-sized monster.<ref name=":2" /> Kota was able to use a device to call the ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'' and escaped with Starkiller. The Gorog then fell into one of Cato Neimoidia's canyons.<ref name="TFU2" /> Such events however didn't kill it as it pass out, but his second heart continued to function.<ref name="TFU2comic" />

===Final demise===
[[File:NothingbutJet.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Boba Fett killing the Gorog]]
While following the wake of destruction caused by Marek's clone, [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and [[Xasha]] found the battered Gorog. The creature revived suddenly and, despite already being grievously injured, aggressively began to attack the two mercenaries. Fett, having scanned the creature, identified a second heart within the Gorog. Fett fired a back-mounted rocket at the Gorog's heart and used his [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] to fly through the gaping wound in the creature's torso, finally killing the beast.<ref name="TFU2comic" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Starkiller_vs_Gorog.png|thumb|left|250px|The Gorog facing Starkiller as seen in ''The Force Unleashed II'' teaser trailer]]
The Gorog first appeared in the teaser trailer of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'', where it faces Starkiller in a gladiatorial arena on Cato Neimoidia, although its appearance differed slightly in comparison to its final design seen in the game.

The Gorog's design was heavily influenced by the [[Gorax/Legends|Gorax]], which was originally created by concept artist [[Ralph McQuarrie]].<ref name=":1" />

In the [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Forced Unleashed II'']] comic, Boba Fett and Xasha find the corpse of the Gorog among the rubble within the suspended [[Bridge city/Legends|bridge city]] of Tarko-se.<ref name="TFU2comic" /> This contradicts other versions of ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'', which depict the creature plummeting from the city during its battle with Starkiller.<ref name="TFU2" />

The third part of the battle with the Gorog, which was set while it was plummeting, was omitted from the [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] version. Also, the Gorog was depicted without its head covering in the Wii version.<ref>''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>
